Central Nervous System
Anatomy
Lateral & 3rd ventricles and CSF Circulation

Quick Overview

This lesson covers two cavities of the ventricular system, the lateral ventricles and the third ventricle, followed by the production, circulation, and final drainage of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). It describes the parts of the lateral ventricle, the walls and communications of the third ventricle, the choroid plexuses and their blood supply, and the path CSF takes from the ventricles to the venous sinuses, including the basis of hydrocephalus.

Complete Lesson Content

Lateral ventricle

There are two lateral ventricles, one in each cerebral hemisphere. Each is a C-shaped cavity lined with ependyma. It communicates with the 3rd ventricle through the interventricular foramen of Monro.

Parts of the lateral ventricle

PartDescription
Anterior hornAnterior extension from the central part into the frontal lobe; lies in front of the interventricular foramen.
Central partLies mostly within the parietal lobe; extends from the interventricular foramen in front to the splenium of the corpus callosum behind.
Posterior hornBackward extension from the central part into the occipital lobe.
Inferior hornContinuation of the main cavity into the temporal lobe; the largest of the three horns.

Choroid plexus

The choroid plexuses of the two lateral ventricles are supplied by the anterior choroidal artery.

Third ventricle

The 3rd ventricle is the cavity of the diencephalon: a midline, slit-like cavity situated between the two thalami and part of the hypothalamus.

Communications

  • With the lateral ventricle through the interventricular foramen of Monro.
  • With the 4th ventricle through the cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius.

Boundaries

WallFormed by
Anterior wallAnterior column of fornix, anterior commissure, lamina terminalis
Posterior wallPineal gland, posterior commissure, cerebral aqueduct
RoofEpendyma stretching between the two thalami, covered by pia mater and invaginated by the choroid plexus of the third ventricle
FloorOptic chiasma, infundibulum, mammillary bodies, posterior perforated substance, tegmentum of the midbrain
Lateral wallThalamus, hypothalamus, hypothalamic groove

Choroid plexus

The choroid plexus of the 3rd ventricle is supplied by the anterior choroidal arteries and choroidal branches of the posterior cerebral artery.

Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)

CSF is present in the ventricular system and in the subarachnoid space surrounding the CNS.

Volume and production

  • Volume: 150 ml in an adult; 30 ml is in the ventricular system and the remainder in the subarachnoid space.
  • Production: 70% by the choroid plexuses into the brain ventricles; 30% by filtration from brain capillaries.

Circulation

  1. CSF is produced mainly in the lateral ventricles and passes through the interventricular foramina (of Monro) into the third ventricle.
  2. Small amounts are added by the third ventricle, and the fluid passes via the cerebral aqueduct into the fourth ventricle.
  3. Small amounts are added by the fourth ventricle. From here, a small amount passes down into the central canal of the spinal cord, while the greater amount leaves via the foramen of Magendie and the foramina of Luschka into the subarachnoid space around the brain and spinal cord.

Final drainage

CSF is drained by the arachnoid villi into the cranial venous sinuses, especially the superior sagittal sinus, to reach the bloodstream. Arachnoid villi coalesce to form arachnoid granulations that project into the superior sagittal sinus; the villi have channels through which CSF drains into the venous sinus.

CSF pressure in the arachnoid villi must exceed venous pressure for drainage to occur. If the opposite happens, the villi collapse, their channels close, and drainage fails.

Hydrocephalus

Hydrocephalus is an abnormal increase in the volume of CSF within the skull. It can result from blockage at some point in CSF circulation, with CSF accumulation and ventricular dilatation above the level of the blockage.

Key Points / Quick Review

Lateral ventricle

  • C-shaped, ependyma-lined; one per hemisphere; opens to 3rd ventricle via foramen of Monro.
  • Anterior horn (frontal), central part (parietal, to splenium), posterior horn (occipital), inferior horn (temporal, largest).
  • Choroid plexus: anterior choroidal artery.

Third ventricle

  • Midline slit between thalami and part of hypothalamus; cavity of the diencephalon.
  • Connects to lateral ventricles (Monro) and 4th ventricle (aqueduct of Sylvius).
  • Anterior: fornix column, anterior commissure, lamina terminalis. Posterior: pineal, posterior commissure, aqueduct.
  • Choroid plexus: anterior choroidal arteries and posterior cerebral choroidal branches.

CSF production and flow

  • 150 ml total; 30 ml in ventricles.
  • 70% choroid plexuses, 30% brain capillary filtration.
  • Lateral, Monro, third, aqueduct, fourth, then Magendie/Luschka to subarachnoid space (small amount to central canal).

Drainage and hydrocephalus

  • Arachnoid villi and granulations drain into cranial venous sinuses, especially the superior sagittal sinus.
  • CSF pressure must exceed venous pressure, otherwise villi collapse.
  • Hydrocephalus: excess CSF; blockage causes dilatation above the blockage.
